title: Iter
tagline: Onchain CLOB+pool DEX: LPs set their own price tolerance, so sandwiche attacks stop
description:
Iter is a decentralized spot exchange that separates the two questions every trading venue has to answer: who supplies the tradable inventory, and how a trade is priced and settled.

Every AMM fused those into a single bonding curve. That is why a Uniswap LP cannot decline a price — the curve fills their capital at whatever price the market pushes it to, all the way down. Onchain order book DEXes fixed settlement but abandoned inventory: their liquidity still comes from professional market makers, not permissionless LPs.

Iter answers both. Settlement is a fully onchain central limit order book, with price-time or size priority chosen per pair at listing. Inventory is a pool layered on top that converts permissionless LP capital into ordinary limit orders on that same book, rather than a second pricing primitive. Every position carries its own slippageLimit, so an LP sets the worst price they will accept. At slippageLimit = 0 a position only ever executes at the reference price, which bounds its worst-case impermanent loss by construction.

Pool trades are priced against a TWAP reference rather than instantaneous spot, so the price an attacker can manufacture inside one block is not the price the pool trades at. In our simulation this cuts same-block sandwich extractability by roughly three orders of magnitude — to negative attacker profit once gas is counted.

Because settlement is an order book, a trade can also add liquidity: it settles whatever it can match and the remainder rests as the trader's own limit order, instead of an AMM route's all-or-nothing revert.

The costs are real and we state them: occasional partial fills when tolerant liquidity is thin, and roughly 6x Uniswap v2's gas per swap, which makes Iter an L2 protocol by construction.
how_its_made: CONTRACTS (Solidity 0.8.24, Foundry). MatchingEngine + Orderbook are the settlement layer: a fully onchain order book in 8-decimal fixed point (DENOM = 1e8), with price-time or size priority selected per pair at listing. src/swap holds the inventory layer — BandPool, PoolBands, BandPositionManager, BandSwapRouter. A "band" is a price tolerance anchored to the orderbook TWAP. The whitepaper described this as a per-position slippageLimit; in the shipped contracts we hoisted it into discrete buckets, because a continuous per-position tolerance had no bucket to be fungible inside. Band is a uint32 tolerance packed alongside shares and an open flag, so a band costs no extra storage slot.
auto_summary: A decentralized exchange project with onchain orderbook settlement, pooled liquidity contracts, and a frontend that includes cross-chain USDC deposit flows.
